A conceptual diagram illustrating industrial location (Weber's triangle concept). A central factory icon. Three arrows point to it from three corners: "Raw Material Source", "Power/Energy Source", and "Market (City)". A truck is shown driving on a road connecting the factory to the market. Labels should clearly show that the factory's location balances the pull of raw materials, power, and market. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background.

A four-part circular infographic showing the four economic sectors. Top-left (Primary): A farmer harvesting crops and an oil rig. Top-right (Secondary): A factory building with smokestacks and a worker welding a car. Bottom-left (Tertiary): A retail shop counter with a cashier and a delivery truck. Bottom-right (Quaternary): A scientist looking through a microscope and a programmer at a multi-monitor computer. Arrows connect them in a cycle to show the flow from raw material to advanced knowledge. Clean flat textbook illustration, white background, clearly labeled.

A simplified world map showing major ocean trade routes. Bold lines for the North Atlantic Route connecting NE USA to Western Europe. A line through the Mediterranean and Red Sea. A line going around the southern tip of Africa. A line across the Pacific Ocean. Small icons for commodities (a cocoa pod in West Africa, an oil barrel in the Middle East, a car in Japan/China) with arrows pointing toward Europe and the USA.
